newsitem.title: UK: S&N seen serving up higher annual profits.
newsitem.headline: S&N seen serving up higher annual profits.

text.p: British brewer and leisure giant Scottish and Newcastle Plc is expected to serve up a solid rise in profits when it unveils annual profits on June 30.

However, analysts, who are looking for pretax profits of between 361 to 380 million stg compared with 308.2 million last time, note that much of the profits rise will have come from the restructuring benefits of Scottish Courage.
The company bought Courage from Australian brewer Fosters in 1995 for 550 million stg and took reorganisation costs of just over 150 million stg as a one off charge against earnings.

"They have had a reasonable integration period from Courage and this will obviously boost these numbers, but on an underlying basis, strategically there are still significant concerns for us," said Phil Hawkins, an analyst at Merrill Lynch.
Analysts are anxious mainly over the company's holiday village business Center Parcs, where a heavy investment programme and weak consumer demand in mainland Europe have held back leisure profits.
During the first half these factors saw profits at Center Parcs fall 11 percent to 44 million stg.
"We are still not convinced over the quality of earnings from Center Parcs and their recovery potential, and therefore the returns on capital still to us are unacceptable," said Hawkins at Merrill.

On the brewing side, where the company is Britain's biggest, selling around 29 pints of every 100 consumed, there are mild concerns over what will happen to volume once a contract with IEL expires in March 1998. IEL will then be able to go into the market and get full retail discount.
"They will lose a significant proportion of volume from that contract, that may well necessitate a further restructuring provision to be taken," said Hawkins at Merrill.
"Not only will S&N get less volume as a result of this, with up to a third of this volume may go to other brewers, they will have to increase the discount to IEL," said Merrill's Hawkins.

Hawkins said that potentially S&N could lose around two hundred thousand barrels and pay a bigger discount on the remainder to IEL. He estimates this could result in a hit of around 10 million stg over the next couple of years.

S&N was obliged by competition authorities to reduce its tied pub estate by 115 to 2,624 following its purchase of Courage. It also agreed to the early release of IEL (Intrepreneur estates Ltd) pub tenants from a supply agreement. It had to release 500 of them by January 1996 and a further 500 by January 1997.
